Subject: MAP: cost sanity check before pilot kickoff

Hi Monica,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. As we lock the MAP milestones I need a short written checklist we can share with Procurement and Engineering to ensure we won’t hit unexpected unit-econ gaps during the two-week pilot. High level context: NovusCare expects ~2M monthly tokens during pilot peak, mostly short queries (~50–120 tokens each) and a 20% subset of longer diagnostic requests (~600 tokens). Target total cost for pilot needs to be < $950/month for inference (our internal cap).

Specific asks: can you confirm realistic tokens/$ at pilot conditions, what cache hit rates we should design for, and the batching/latency tradeoffs we should accept? Procurement wants these on the MAP so they can sign off on the pilot payment.

Ethan

NovusCare

Ethan — thanks for the clear constraints. Below is a concise MAP-ready checklist and the acceptance criteria we recommend for the pilot. I attached the MAP workbook (novuscare_map_v2.xlsx) with the same numbers and a quick sensitivity tab.

MAP cost acceptance checklist (pilot window: 2 weeks)
- Consumption baseline: validate 2M monthly token-equivalent within pilot traffic profile (2-week sample extrapolation). Acceptance: measured token volume within ±15% of projection.
- Tokens / $ (pilot-adjusted): expected range $0.28–$0.45 per 1k tokens depending on batching and quantization profile. Acceptance: average tokens/$ must be within 10% of the MAP projection.
- Caching: enable prefix/KV caching for conversational reuse. Pilot gate: cache hit rate >= 22% across sampled traffic. If below, customer must accept higher costs or Redwood will enable additional caching heuristics and re-run.
- Batching vs latency: we will test two configs — conservative (batch size target 8, prioritizes latency) and aggressive (batch size target 32, prioritizes cost). Acceptance: p95 generation latency must remain <= 450ms on conservative; cost/1k should improve >= 25% on aggressive with p95 <= 850ms.
- Regression checks: use 500-case eval set from NovusCare (shared Drive link) — generation quality must not degrade >2% on BLEU/ROUGE surrogate metrics used in our eval harness.
- Rollback trigger: if tokens/$ exceed MAP projection by >15% for 48h contiguous window, auto-fail and trigger canary to smaller model variant.

Pilot deliverables & timeline (MAP milestones)
- Day 0 (kickoff): install telemetry + MAP workbook snapshot (we’ll collect 48h of baseline).
- Day 3–4: preliminary token volume and cache-hit analysis; initial batching experiment (conservative).
- Day 7: run aggressive batching experiment and record p95/p99 latency, tokens/$.
- Day 10: final evaluation run (500-case eval + traffic sample) and MAP sign-off recommendation.

Attachments: novuscare_map_v2.xlsx (MAP workbook) — includes sensitivity, traffic mix, and cost per 1k tokens by config.

Next steps: if this looks good I’ll loop Procurement and schedule the telemetry install. Ben / Karthik — any additions on the experiment parameters?

— Monica
Principal Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Following up with the numbers we’ll include in the MAP workbook (also in Drive). Key assumptions we should surface to NovusCare Procurement: 
- Pilot token mix assumption: 80% short (50–120 tokens), 20% long (avg 600 tokens). If their distribution shifts to 60/40 we project tokens/$ to worsen ~28%.
- Baseline kernel/throughput (NVIDIA A100-equivalent): conservative batching (8) yields ~6.1k tokens/sec per GPU; aggressive batching (32) yields ~14.8k tokens/sec per GPU. These map to cost deltas in the workbook.
- Latency/queueing: conservative config keeps median latency ~120–220ms and p95 ~350–420ms in our lab; aggressive pushes median to ~250–420ms and p95 to ~700–900ms depending on live variance.
- Billing note: tokens measured are input+output; we model total token cost in the workbook and show 3 quantization tiers (fp16, int8, int4-quant-proxy).

I’ll add a short 'sensitivity' tab that shows tokens/$ across cache hit rates from 10% to 40% and batching targets 8/16/32. That will make the acceptance gate math explicit for Procurement.

Karthik
Sr. Performance Engineer
